dismissed.why_not_material: Moderate severity evidence-quality overreach about week-4 viral kinetics. While this promotes an interim biomarker rather than the SVR12 primary endpoint, it describes supportive open-label lead-in data from the same Phase 2 study. Per principle #3, citing early uncontrolled kinetics alongside a controlled trial is standard biotech promotion, not misrepresentation of the catalyst's basis. The claim does not substitute the biomarker for the registered endpoint or overstate the trial's design.

Minor operational masking. Timeline guidance issued Nov 2024 for 'early December' readout after a 5-month completion slip. This is timeline softening, not concealment of negative efficacy data. Does not signal masking of likely clinical miss.

Minor operational masking. May 2024 guidance of 'second half 2024' when registry showed June 2024, issued weeks before a slip to November. This reflects enrollment/operational delays, not efficacy concealment.
Minor operational masking. Duplicate of avir_019 concern—timeline softening around operational delays, not a signal of data quality issues or efficacy masking.

analyst_note: All four refuted findings relate to the catalyst Phase 2 HCV trial (bemnifosbuvir + ruzasvir 8-week regimen, NCT05904470). The single moderate finding (avir_023) promoted week-4 viral kinetics as 'supportive' of the 8-week regimen rather than relying solely on the SVR12 primary endpoint; however, this constitutes normal early-stage color commentary on lead-in data, not substitution or endpoint manipulation. The three minor findings document timeline drift—completion slipped from June to November 2024, with guidance softening from specific dates to 'second half' ranges—but operational delays are not clinical masking. No company-level dishonesty findings were identified. The marketing reflects standard promotional enthusiasm without material misrepresentation of the catalyst trial's design, endpoints, or data integrity.
